findings.summary: Bind pointer accessors by executing the pin's path converter over recording stand-ins instead of rebuilding its regex literals in the lowerer.
Carry the pin's pick filter on the pick request (hook parameter and shared candidate collector) instead of an engine global with an RAII scope; decide the pick-source exclusion once per pass.
Own the node visibility and base-colour transform accessors in the generated loader beside their tables; drop the unconditional flow-graph helpers.
Join the interactivity feature in the per-asset loop so an asset-only reach re-renders the generated-source table and CMake.
Assert the coordinator's tick closure body instead of the unused tickFlowGraph, the pin's pointer-identity guard, and pickAsyncImpl's two filter arms.
Admit an asset's flowGraphRuntimes read only directly under await; the asset alone reaches the feature.
Carry parser values as plain data, keep one BABYLON_flow_graph refusal, and drop the unread dataOut serialization.
Share the dynamic-import registry parser with the node-particle lowerer and hoist Vec2d, Vec4d and Color4d into runtime.hpp.
Use the shared operator and Math tables and the identifier sanitizer; memoize pinned helper lookups; delete dead opaque constructors and the string variable arm.
Walk the runtime list in place in the coordinator tick, visit pointer runtimes without allocating, and resolve the picked mesh's node once per pick.
Count a parenthesized shape once in expectShapeCount.
Fill the interactivity tables at the end of the load under the extension predicate and copy node visibility by assignment.
Share one upstream store and one pinned parse across the flow-graph tests; spread the registry environment before the check tool's frame window.
State the Calculator's residual from measurements in the registry and narrow the TODO rows it touches.
Extract one partial evaluator shared by the node-particle and flow-graph lowerers.
findings.blockedBy: The two evaluators differ in value semantics (loose null equality in the node-particle arm, strict equality in the flow-graph arm); a shared core needs both generated trees proven byte-identical, a measurement not yet taken.

findings.summary: Emit flow-graph node functions as members of the generated Runtime class.
findings.blockedBy: The emitter's two-pass function table (prototypes, then bodies) has no per-graph class form; SceneState::flow_graphs keeps the non-template base either way.
